facts.fact: The Labari Journal reports that Ghana's World Bank-funded eJustice system, meant to automate court registry filing through to execution of decisions, is still being rolled out and an IMF 2024 governance report says it has "stalled".
A Judicial Service of Ghana document from 2022, cited by The Labari Journal, put the number of cases on the eJustice system at 61,000+, up from 58,495 the previous year.

systems.tiers: Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, High and Circuit Courts in regional capitals and Tema (planned)

note: The document describes only a VAT collection mechanism for foreign digital services starting 2026-10-15; it states nothing about this study's questions.
The system is the human rights commission's, not a court's; its rollout is stalled.

facts.fact: Ghana's e-justice system, a USD 3.3 million part of the World Bank-funded e-Transform project, registers cases, allocates them to courts and judges and manages judges' calendars at court registries, with about 75,829 cases filed as of January 2025 per the Judicial Service, per 3News.
Lawyers file cases and legal processes online through the e-justice platform, with the Ghana Card required, per 3News.

systems.tiers: registries of the higher courts; Greater Accra

note: Only a forward announcement on 29 July 2026 of e-filing and court automation from 1 October 2026; no system stated built, piloted or in service.
